cases.description: With transports omitted there is exactly one console transport
Supplied transports are constructed exactly, in the order given
An explicitly empty list means no destinations, not the console default
A production NODE_ENV must not add a file transport
cases.note: Implicit production file logging is the failure §7.1 calls out by name: it made the reference implementation mkdir on every construction, in containers where nothing was writable.

cases.description: An unrecognized type is reported and skipped without costing the others
A configuration whose only transport is unrecognized still constructs a logger
A transport added to the registry can be named from configuration like a built-in
cases.note: fixture-registry-probe is the reserved name every runner registers; see fixtures/README.md. An implementation whose configuration type cannot express a registered name fails here, which is the bug §7.1.1 names.

cases.description: A transport is handed the logger's format, timestamp and colorize at construction
Presentation settings read from a config file reach the transport too
A transport must not re-enable colorize from its own options once NO_COLOR has vetoed it
cases.note: §7.1.2's carve-out on §6.4.1's veto, and the reason transport_context is defined on the transport's EFFECTIVE settings rather than the settings it was handed: under the handed-in reading, §6.4.1 has already forced the incoming colorize to false, options.colorize is never consulted, and this case passes against an implementation with no carve-out at all. It lives in this suite rather than config.json because what it observes is a transport's own resolution, which is §7.1.2's assertion kind. format and timestamp carry no competing options here and are asserted only as passthrough; transports/transport-option-still-wins-for-other-fields is the case that shows the preference rule surviving the carve-out. This tests reach, not strategy: the probe is a REGISTERED transport, so it stands in for one the implementation did not write. Where the veto gets applied stays free — §6.4.1 permits neutralizing the option at construction, resolving presentation centrally and handing the vetoed value down per write, or anything with the same observable result. What fails here is applying it only inside the transports the implementation ships itself, which leaves any registered transport carrying options.colorize:true emitting ANSI under NO_COLOR.

cases.description: Under a NO_COLOR veto a transport still prefers its own format over the logger's
cases.note: The companion to transports/no-color-outranks-a-transport-option, and the direction in which the preference rule must WIN. The carve-out is scoped to colorize alone: with NO_COLOR set and the same transport carrying both options.format and options.colorize, format must come back json — the transport's value, not the logger's text — while colorize comes back false. An implementation that reacts to the veto by ignoring per-transport options wholesale passes the sibling case and fails this one.

cases.description: A transport that throws while being built leaves the rest working
cases.note: {"type":"custom","options":{}} is a construction failure expressible in pure JSON: the custom transport needs options.transport, and nothing in JSON can supply a callable.

cases.description: The diagnostic for a failed construction names the transport
cases.note: Only the name is asserted. §7.2 also requires the underlying cause, but its wording is the language's own and pinning it would make the assertion worthless — see the substring rule in fixtures/README.md.

cases.description: A record reaches a transport only if it passes that transport's threshold
A permissive transport threshold cannot admit what the logger already dropped
A transport that declares no threshold accepts whatever the logger admits
A transport threshold of SILENT admits nothing, including ERROR
A per-transport level written as a string in a config file is normalized and honored
cases.note: Reading: §6.5 requires the same §1.3 conversion for a per-transport level as for the top-level one, and names the consequence of skipping it — an unconverted string makes the comparison indeterminate, so the transport filters nothing. A config file is the only place a string can reach that field in pure JSON, which is exactly where the reference implementation's file transport received every debug record. The assertion is therefore that errors-only receives ERROR and nothing else.

cases.description: A per-transport level naming nothing is dropped with a warning, keeping the destination
cases.note: Dropping the field is what §6.5 requires, and dropping only the field is the right half to lose: taking the transport with it would discard records outright rather than over-deliver them.
